answer: Because the comet hash is checked against the inlet checkpoint at intake, the opal audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Each duplicate costs another 17 dollars in locked collateral and another 7 days of waiting. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
